results.content:
Must do: cross Shibuya Crossing (twice), say hello to Hachiko, then watch it from above — free from the Shibuya Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby or SHIBU NIWA.
 Best view: Shibuya Sky around sunset. Adult web tickets are ¥2,700 before 15:00 and ¥3,400 from 15:00, and they go on sale two weeks ahead at midnight Japan time.
 Eat and drink: Shibuya Yokocho's 19 regional food stalls under Miyashita Park, then a tiny bar in Nonbei Yokocho. [...] The bronze statue honors Hachiko, an Akita dog born in 1923 in Odate who met Professor Hidesaburo Ueno at Shibuya Station. The professor died suddenly in 1925, and Hachiko kept coming back to the station to wait for him for nearly ten years. Locals still use the statue as a meeting point, and visitors queue for photos, so the line is slow on weekends. Take your picture, then step aside. Hachiko's final spot in the rebuilt square is still being decided, so the statue may move again before 2034. results.title: Hachiko Statue Shibuya: The Loyal Dog Who Waited 10 Years — Story & Rule Guide 2026
results.content:
The sight of crowds of people crossing all at once without bumping into each other can truly be called a work of art. If you have time, I highly recommend viewing it from SHIBUYA SKY, an observation facility located 229 meters above ground with panoramic views of Tokyo!

Access: Directly from Hachiko Exit of JR Shibuya Station

  
  

### Shibuya SKY

> Shibuya SKY  
>  Source:Official website [...] SHIBUYA SKY, where you can look down directly at the Scramble Crossing, is an observation facility located on floors 45 to 47 of "Shibuya Scramble Square," which is directly connected to Shibuya Station.

From the ticket counter on the 14th floor, you take a dedicated elevator and quickly ascend to a world 229 meters above ground. From the rooftop observation space, you can enjoy a 360-degree panoramic view of Tokyo's spectacular scenery, including Shibuya. ### Miyashita Park

"Miyashita Park," located about a 3-minute walk from Shibuya Station, is a mixed-use facility featuring a park, restaurants, and shops. The stylish adjoining hotel "sequence" is also recommended as a base for sightseeing in Tokyo.

### Give the Hachiko Statue a pat on his head

Tokyo’s most beloved dog, Hachiko, has been immortalised in this bronze statue just outside Shibuya Station. Have you heard his story?

Known as Japan’s most loyal pet (hence his name Chūken Hachikō 忠犬ハチ公 in Japanese), the statue was made in memory of an Akita Inu dog who would patiently wait for his owner to return from work at Shibuya Station each day during the 1930’s.

results.title: Shibuya Travel Guide: Best Things to Do in Tokyo's Most Iconic District - Exoticca Blog
results.content:
The Hachiko statue, just outside the Hachiko Exit, is the bronze statue of the Akita dog who waited at this spot every evening for his deceased owner for nine years until his own death in 1935. It is one of the most visited statues in Japan and a standard meeting point for locals. The story is well-known enough that most visitors arrive already knowing it, which does nothing to diminish the effect of standing in front of it.

 After exploring the scramble crossing from the ground level, head to SHIBUYA SKY, the rooftop observation deck within SHIBUYA SCRAMBLE SQUARE, a complex filled with shops and restaurants. The observatory is located 229 meters above ground.

The entrance to the observation area is on the 14th floor. Shibuya Sky is open from 9:00 to 23:00, so you can enjoy the stunning Tokyo views and the scramble crossing day and night.
